chapter: Moten band, arranging and the guitar
title: Teaching Charlie Christian the downstroke in Oklahoma City
summary: In 1937 Durham showed Christian in a pool hall how to play single-note downstrokes like a horn, and Christian picked it up in minutes.

story.theme_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section: instruments and players
story.community_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section's changing role

blocks.x: It must be late '30s. Did you know Charlie Christian?
Got the first guitar with him.
Utah?
Yeah.
Well, now, when did you do that?
That was in Oklahoma City, when I was with Basie's band -- Benny Morton.
Yeah.
And we used to play there on location, somewhere.
Where were you playing?

That's what I've been trying to figure out here. James Richmond was in the band, Buster Smith, and that's when Charlie started to playing. And we used to go down to the pool hall every day, James Richmond would follow, on the pool hall, and I was down there,and Charlie Christian came in, you know. And he had an old acoustic guitar. (Inaudible.) He say, how do you sound like that saxophone? I say, if you play the downstroke, Charlie, you gotta be fast or it don't never come out. And I say, and you're going to always get a staccato instead of a legato, and you'll sound Willie Smith. That's what I was doing. And -- I don't care what kind of guitar it is, so he said, well, I play the piano. I say, what are you doing? He say, well, I'm playing a little piano. He was playing a little piano, he was trying to play piano.

And I showed him, and he took the guitar. And he sat down and he did it, and in a few minutes, he had it. I say, both this guy put everbody out of business in a few months. I say, you got it, and he picked right up on it. Must had been playing a little somewhere.
Yes, he --
Yeah, he's probably (inaudible). And I say -- and so, that was in 1937. So I was around there three

or four weeks, and he hung around with me for a few of them things. I didn't have to teach him much. Just told him -- I said, that's the secret of the -- sound like a horn, down-stroke. And he started playing with that downstroke.
And later on, he told me, he's playing that, it sounds just like you. And, sure enough, the next thing I know, he's with (inaudible). I say, and now I'd like to sound like him a little bit.
Yeah, well, he must have developed very rapidly then.
Yeah, he did, when he has time. I guess you can do that, because he wasn't bothered with music, it's just bothered with playing.
Yeah, yeah.
I just wonder if he ever did read. I don't even know if he --
I don't know, I don't know at all. But you'd think he did.
Well, he wouldn't have to read to play that part that Benny Goodman had.
Not the kind of stuff he played with Benny Goodman?
No, he wouldn't have to read to play that.
No? Well, now, what about--
All them rhythms they can make up (unintelligible).
